actions.label: Test pairing key edit and reload

reproduce.expected_result: Accepted changes persist and reconnect; rejected changes preserve old state and expose the actual failure instead of appearing accepted.
prerequisites: Two disposable Windows endpoints with matching PowerToys versions and test-owned pairing settings.
Retain existing configuration; record equality and operation outcome only, not key values.
steps: Connect the endpoints using the supported UI and a test-owned key.
Apply a different valid key through the supported UI; confirm whether the operation is accepted before checking persistence.
Reload settings and fully restart both endpoints; verify the accepted key remains effective.
Repeat invalid input and a deliberately rejected pairing operation; confirm existing state remains unchanged.
reproduce.version_requirement: Reported/current release and current development build

judgment.recommended_action: Run a two-endpoint key edit/reload regression on a disposable setup, then identify the exact surviving producer before designing a new change.
evidence: The complete discussion reports that editing a key can leave the persisted value stale and that manual replacement/reset has mixed results across versions. No secret keys are needed to reproduce this contract.

The contributor linked51377 and described the live Encryption.MyKey versus stored Settings.MyKey mismatch. Live51377 is closed/unmerged; its author says it was superseded without naming a replacement in that reply.

Current main no longer has the cited classic UpdateKey producer; ConnectToMachine assigns both Setting.Values.MyKey and Encryption.MyKey. That source observation does not establish a released fix for every historical failure.
Some participants report the standalone legacy MWB product and others report later generic pairing failures; those are not automatically the same producer defect.
judgment.rationale: Do not advertise the closed PR as active or shipped, and do not duplicate its obsolete classic-form patch. Test key acceptance, persistence and reload on the reported/current product while separating a stale key from an IPC/signer rejection. Preserve user configuration and never request actual keys.

proposed_fixes.title: Verify MWB pairing-key persistence across reload
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Historical evidence supports live-versus-persisted key divergence; current main uses a different coordinated update path, so persistence failure in that path is unproven.
verification: A valid accepted key stays equal in stored/runtime state after reload and both endpoints reconnect.
Invalid input leaves both stored and live values unchanged.
Existing protected/service-mode and rejected IPC requests must not silently overwrite pairing state.
plan: Use test-owned endpoints and keys; record only equality/outcome, never actual keys.
Exercise accepted key update, settings reload and full restart on each endpoint; distinguish rejection before apply from accepted-but-not-persisted state.
If divergence survives on current code, correct its identified update/persistence transaction and add valid/invalid/reload coverage; do not restore a removed classic producer.

confidence.rationale: Multiple detailed historical persistence reports exist, but the old producer changed and current-version recurrence is not independently demonstrated.

fix_assessment.rationale: A specific persistence contract and source evolution warrant reproduction, but the old implementation target is obsolete and no active covering replacement was established.
